reference_steps: Raw materials were precisely weighed according to stoichiometric ratios.
Materials were ball milled for 8 hours using ethanol as dispersion medium.
Mixed raw materials were dried and calcined at 850°C for 4 hours.

Obtained powder was dried, ground, and compressed into disk with diameter of 8 mm under pressure of 250 MPa.
Ceramics were sintered at 1100°C for 4 hours.
For electrical property testing, both sides were polished and coated with silver or platinum electrodes.
Samples were immersed in silicone oil at 180°C and electric field of 150-200 kV/cm was applied for 30 minutes for polarization.

method.reference: mixed oxide method with composite fabrication

reference_steps: BZT powder was prepared by calcining barium carbonate, zirconium dioxide and titanium dioxide at 1200°C for 2 h using mixed oxide method.
BZT powder was pressed into disc shape of ~15 mm diameter and thickness of ~1.5 mm at applied pressure of ~85 MPa.
BZT discs were sintered at 1450°C for 2 h.
BZT discs (dimension ~12 mm and thickness ~1.5 mm) were poled using electric field of 1.5 kV/mm at 50°C for 30 min in silicone oil chamber.
Poled BZT ceramic was cut using diamond saw in parallel direction along polarization axis using cut and fill method.
Mixtures of Portland cement powder, water (w/c ratio 0.35), epoxy resin and hardener (volume ratio 7.5) were prepared as matrix phase.
Mixture was filled into cut areas of BZT ceramic to create 1-3 connectivity composites with 40, 50, and 60 vol% BZT and 0, 3, 5, and 7 vol% epoxy resin.
Samples were cured in controlled chamber at 60°C for 5 days at 98% RH.
test_steps: Calcined barium carbonate, zirconium dioxide, and titanium dioxide at 1200 °C for 2 h
Pressed BZT powder into a disc shape of ~15 mm diameter and ~1.5 mm thickness at ~85 MPa
Sintered BZT discs at 1450 °C for 2 h
Poled BZT discs using an electric field of 1.5 kV/mm at 50 °C for 30 min in a silicone oil chamber
Cut poled BZT ceramic using a diamond saw in a parallel direction along with the polarization axis
Mixed Portland cement powder, water, epoxy resin, and hardener as the matrix phase with w/c ratio of 0.35 and epoxy resin to hardener volume ratio of 7.5
Filled the mixture into the cut areas of the BZT ceramic
Cured samples in a controlled chamber at 60 °C for 5 days at 98 %RH

reference_steps: 0.011 mol Bi(NO3)3 and 0.01 mol Fe(NO3)3·9H2O were dissolved into 100 mL deionized water to obtain 0.11 M bismuth nitrate and 0.1 M iron nitrate solutions.
3 mL nitric acid (68%) was added gradually to bismuth nitrate solution during stirring until completely dissolved.
Two solutions were mixed and 0.02 mol triammonium citrate was added as complexing agent and stirred for 30 minutes.
Gel was obtained by continuous stirring at 90°C until water completely evaporated.
Gel was calcined at 550°C for 2 hours to obtain pure phase BFO powder particles.
10 mL of 0.3 M cadmium chloride solution was added to 50 mL of 0.1 M sodium citrate solution and stirred at room temperature for 20 minutes.
3 mL concentrated ammonia (NH3·H2O 28%) and 10 mL of 0.6 M thiourea solution were added in sequence.
Mixed solution was reacted in water bath at 60°C for 2.5 hours.
Precipitate was collected by centrifugation, rinsed with deionized water and anhydrous ethanol, and dried at 60°C.
test_steps: Dissolve Bi(NO3)3 and Fe(NO3)3·9H2O in deionized water to obtain 0.11 M bismuth nitrate and 0.1 M iron nitrate solutions.
Add 3 mL of nitric acid (68%) to the bismuth nitrate solution under constant stirring until completely dissolved.
Mix the two solutions and add 0.02 mol of triammonium citrate as the complexing agent, stir for 30 min.
Obtain gel by continuous stirring at 90°C until water is completely evaporated.
Calcinate the gel at 550°C for 2 h to obtain pure phase BFO powder particles.
For CdS nanosheets: Add 10 mL of 0.3 M cadmium chloride solution to 50 mL of 0.1 M sodium citrate solution and stir at room temperature for 20 min.
Add 3 mL of concentrated ammonia (28%) and 10 mL of 0.6 M thiourea solution sequentially.
React the mixed solution in a water bath at 60°C for 2.5 h.
Collect the precipitate by centrifugation, rinse with deionized water and anhydrous ethanol, and dry at 60°C to obtain CdS nanosheets.
For BFO/CdS composites: Weigh 0.6 g of BFO into 60 mL of 0.1 M sodium citrate solution, add 1.38 mL of 0.3 M cadmium chloride solution (10 wt% of BFO), and stir at room temperature for 3 h.
Add 3.6 mL of concentrated ammonia (28%) and 1.38 mL of 0.9 M thiourea solution slowly.
React at 60°C in a water bath for 2.5 h.
Collect the precipitate, rinse with deionized water and anhydrous ethanol, and dry at 60°C to obtain 10% CdS/BiFeO3 (BC10) samples.
Adjust cadmium chloride and thiourea solution volumes to obtain 20% and 30% CdS/BiFeO3 composites (BC20 and BC30).

reference_steps: MgO, Sc2O3 and Nb2O5 were used to synthesize precursors MgNb2O6 at 1000°C and ScNbO4 at 1150°C.
MgNb2O6, ScNbO4, TiO2 and PbO powders were weighed according to stoichiometric proportion with 2 mol% extra PbO added.
Alcohol and oxide powders were mixed in 1:1 ratio by wet-milling for 24 hours.
Combined powder was calcined at 800-850°C for 2 hours.
Calcined mixture was mixed again for 12 hours.
Powder was conglutinated with polyvinyl alcohol solution and pressed into tablets under 8 MPa.
PVA was burned off at 550°C for 2 hours.
Ceramic tablets were covered by powders with same composition and sintered at 1200-1280°C for 4 hours.
Polished samples were coated with silver electrodes on both sides.
Samples were poled at 130°C for 15 minutes under 30 kV/cm electric field.

family.reference: Barium Calcium Zirconate Titanate or BCZT

reference_steps: Raw precursors Ba(CH3COO)2, Ca(NO3)2·4H2O, Zr(NO3)4·5H2O, Ti(OC4H9)4, La(NO3)3·nH2O, and Tm(NO3)3·5H2O were added to an Erlenmeyer flask.
Ethanol was added to react for 3 hours to obtain polymer solutions.
Solutions were placed in oven at 120°C for 10 hours.
Materials were calcined at 900°C for 2 hours in muffle furnace to form precursor powders.
Powders were mixed with 2 wt% polyvinyl alcohol (PVA) as organic binder with weight ratio of PVA and powders 1:120.
Mixture was formed into disks with diameter of 20 mm under 20 MPa pressure with retention time of 150 seconds.
Disks were embedded in alumina and sintered at 1300°C for 4 hours in air using heating rate of 5°C/min.

Formed into disks with a diameter of 20 mm under 20 MPa pressure with a retention time of 150 s.
